frames.narration: An application writes user:42 = 'Maya' and sends it to any node, here D. D hashes the key, walks the ring and finds the preference list: A, C and E.
Gossip told D a few seconds ago that E is down. This cluster uses N = 3 with W = 2, so one failure is tolerable.
D sends the write to all three replicas. A and C store it, in their commit log first and then in memory, and acknowledge.
Two acknowledgements arrived, which is W = 2, so D answers the application: success. E has not seen the write. D keeps a hint saying 'this was meant for E'.
Now the application reads user:42. D asks the replicas that are up. With R = 2, it needs two answers.
Both answer with v7. Any two of the three replicas include at least one that stored the write (2 + 2 is more than 3), so the newest value is always among the answers. D returns 'Maya'.
E comes back. Gossip announces it, and whoever holds the hint hands over the missed write.
In the background, the replicas compare small hash trees of their data and find nothing different. If any hint had been lost, this check would have found the missing key and copied it.
